title: Applied ML evals: integrated onboarding, prompt sets, quantization, guardrails, and regression playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation lifecycle: eval harness usage, prompt set and benchmark management, model onboarding guidance, quality guardrails, quantization profile creation, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs, and applied-ML owners responsible for model serving and release quality.

Goals

- Provide a single, reproducible process for evaluating models before and after deployment.
- Reduce production regressions by standardizing prompt sets, metrics, and triage flows.
- Ensure quantization and inference optimizations preserve quality within defined thresholds.
- Define ownership, SLOs, and automated checks that integrate into CI/CD.

Scope

Includes: prompt set curation, end-to-end eval harness runs, per-model quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and the regression triage workflow. Excludes: model training and research experiments (see research notebooks).

Owners and Roles

- Owner: Applied ML Platform (engineering).
- Primary contacts: Aisha Patel (applied-ml lead), Diego Morales (eval harness), Lena Schmidt (model onboarding).
- Secondary: Serving Runtime (for perf/latency concerns), SRE (alerting, capacity).

Key Definitions

- Eval harness: automated test runner for prompt sets, metrics collection, and drift detection.
- Prompt set: curated collection of examples representing key product intents and edge cases.
- Guardrail: a configured threshold or test that defines acceptable quality for a model/version.
- Quantization profile: settings and validation artifacts used to reduce model size/latency while preserving quality.
- Regression: any measurable drop in a guardrail metric beyond configured tolerance after a change.

High-level Process (overview)

1. Model onboarding request submitted (Model Owner fills onboarding template).
2. Define prompt sets and target metrics (functional & safety & e2e latency).
3. Baseline evaluation using eval harness on floating-point (FP16/FP32) model.
4. If quantization is planned, generate quantized variants and run quantization validation suite.
5. Promote candidate to staging with rollout and canary tests (A/B).
6. Monitor guardrails in production; if regression detected, trigger triage.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)

1. Create Model Onboarding doc (required fields): model name, architecture, training data summary, intended product routes, expected latency, and cost targets.
2. Attach baseline eval harness report (see example below).
3. Provide prompt sets: at minimum "core-intents", "safety-cases", "edge-cases", and "regression-seed-set".
4. Propose initial quantization profile (if applicable): target dtype, per-layer exceptions, calibration dataset.
5. Schedule canary window and list rollout owners and rollback criteria.
6. Request security and compliance review if customer-sensitive data is involved.

Prompt set curation guidelines

- Size & composition: aim for 200-1,000 examples for primary prompt sets; smaller targeted sets (20-100) for edge cases and regression seeds.
- Labels & metadata: include intent_tag, difficulty, expected_output_hash, and scenario notes.
- Coverage matrix: ensure coverage across product features, languages, and failure modes.
- Versioning: store prompt sets in the eval harness repo and tag with model-version and date.

Example prompt set metadata (CSV / YAML accepted)

| field | description | required | example |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| id | unique id | yes | core-00123 |
| intent_tag | product intent | yes | summarize-article |
| difficulty | easy/medium/hard | yes | hard |
| expected_output_hash | hash of canonical output | no | abcd1234 |
| language | ISO code | yes | en-US |

Eval harness: required runs and metrics

- Required runs: baseline (FP), quantized (if applicable), staged canary (live synthetic), regression seed runs.
- Standard metrics collected per prompt set: exact-match (EM), normalized-levenshtein, BLEU, embedding-similarity (cosine), toxicity score, and latency P50/P95/P99.
- Drift and distribution checks: token length distribution, prompt embedding centroid distance, and answer entropy.

Minimum automated checks for CI

- Run full eval harness on PRs that change generation logic or model variant mapping.
- Fail CI if any required guardrail drops beyond tolerance (see Guardrails table).
- Upload run artifacts (JSON outputs, metrics, logs) to the eval artifacts store using the standard naming convention: modelname-version-YYYYMMDD-run.json.

Guardrails and thresholds

| guardrail_name | metric | baseline | tolerance | action |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Core EM | exact-match on core-intents | 0.82 | -0.02 absolute | block promote if breach |
| Safety (toxicity) | toxicity score (avg) | 0.03 | +0.01 absolute | block + safety review |
| Latency | P95 inference latency | 120ms | +30ms absolute | flag for perf review; canary restrict |
| Embedding sim | cosine sim on retrieval QA | 0.78 | -0.03 absolute | require human eval |

Quantization profile creation and validation

- Profiles must include: target dtype (int8/4-bit/FP16), per-layer exclusions, calibration dataset identifier, representative sequence lengths, and expected performance uplift.
- Validation steps (automated):
  1. Apply quantization profile to model build.
  2. Run quantization validation suite (prompt sets + calibration checks).
  3. Compare key metrics to FP baseline and check against guardrail tolerances.
  4. If tolerance exceeded, iterate on profile: adjust per-layer exceptions or fallback layers.

Example quantization profile snippet (YAML)

profile_name: low-latency-int8
target_dtype: int8
excluded_layers: [lm_head, embedding_norm]
calibration_dataset: calibration-2026-06
representative_seq_lengths: [32, 128, 512]
expected_latency_reduction: "~35%"

Note: YAML above is an example to be stored in the quantization-profiles repo.

Regression triage playbook (when a guardrail breach occurs)

1. Alerting: automated alert posts to #applied-ml-regressions with summary (model, metric, delta, run-id, link to artifacts).
2. Triage owner assignment: on-call applied-ml engineer is page owner; model owner must acknowledge within 2 hours.
3. Initial triage (within 4 hours):
   - Re-run failing evals to rule out transient infra issues.
   - Compare raw outputs against baseline run (diff JSON).
   - Classify regression: data drift, model-change, quantization-artifact, or evaluation-bug.
4. Mitigation options depending on class:
   - Evaluation-bug: fix harness or metric calculation; re-run.
   - Quantization-artifact: revert to previous quantized profile or use per-layer fallbacks.
   - Model-change: rollback model version and open RFC with release owners.
   - Data drift: update prompt sets, schedule retest, and consider model retrain.
5. Postmortem and action items: add to regression-triage index, assign owners, define rollout plan, and monitor until metrics recover.

Severity matrix and SLAs

- Sev-1 (critical): core EM drop > 4% absolute on core-intents OR safety breach that increases toxic outputs by >0.05 absolute. Response: immediate rollback or mitigation; pager.
- Sev-2 (high): guarded metric drop between 2-4% absolute OR latency P95 increase above 2x baseline. Response: on-call response within 1 hour.
- Sev-3 (medium): small metric regressions within tolerance or isolated to non-core prompt sets. Response: investigate during business hours.

Operational integrations and dashboards

- Dashboards: per-model guardrail summary, prompt-set trend lines, quantization impact view (delta vs baseline), and alert feed.
- Logs and artifacts: all eval runs stored in artifact-bucket with tags; link artifacts in alert messages.
- CI hooks: pre-deploy check that runs eval harness on canary dataset and gates promotion.

Communication and rollout guidance

- Canary duration: minimum 24 hours for low-risk models; 72 hours for customer-facing high-SLA models.
- Rollout increment: start with 5% traffic, increase to 25% then 100% if guardrails pass.
- Communication template: include model-version, owner, canary metrics, dominant failure modes, and rollback criteria.

Catalogs and storage locations

- Prompt sets repo: git@redwood:evals/prompt-sets.git (tag with model/version).
- Quantization profiles repo: git@redwood:evals/quant-profiles.git.
- Eval artifacts: s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/{model}/{version}/{run_id}.json.

Appendix: Example CI command

# Run full eval harness for model v1.2 on core-intents and safety sets
eval-harness run --model redwood-llm-v1.2 --prompt-sets core-intents,safety-cases --output s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/redwood-llm-v1.2/${RUN_ID}.json --config configs/ci-suite.yaml

Appendix: Example artifact file naming convention

model: redwood-llm-v1.2
version: 2026-07-01
run_id: 20260715-0245
file: redwood-llm-v1.2-20260715-0245.json

Frequently asked questions

Q: When should we allow small quality regressions in exchange for latency/cost gains?
A: Product and model owner must approve a formal tradeoff, captured in the onboarding doc. Tolerances must be encoded in the quantization profile and signed off by owner and SRE if latency/cost impacts infra.

Q: Who approves new prompt sets or changes to core-intents?
A: Model owner must propose changes; the evaluation reviewer (applied-ML reviewer) must sign off after running the eval harness and verifying no latent regressions.
